claim.cause: When args parameter is empty, wrap_text() returns an empty string and doesn't apply the initial_indent prefix, so the usage line is not printed.

feedback.approach: I explored the repository, reproduced the issue with a simple test script, then examined the write_usage() method in formatting.py. I identified that wrap_text("") returns an empty string, causing the usage_prefix to never be written. I implemented a minimal fix that checks if args is empty and writes the prefix directly in that case.
feedback.key_step: Testing that TextWrapper.fill("") returns an empty string, which revealed that initial_indent is not applied when the text parameter is empty.
feedback.wasted_effort: Time spent understanding the indentation format string behavior and fixing the test case once (the first indentation test failed because I misunderstood that indentation only applies when prefix < current_indent), but this was necessary to ensure correctness.

claim.cause: wrap_text returns empty string for empty args, omitting the initial_indent which contained the usage prefix

feedback.approach: I reproduced the issue with the provided code snippet, then examined the HelpFormatter.write_usage method to understand its logic. I tested how wrap_text behaves with empty strings versus non-empty strings, which revealed that wrap_text returns an empty string when given empty input, even with a non-empty initial_indent parameter.
feedback.key_step: Testing wrap_text directly showed it returns an empty string for empty args, not including the initial_indent. This revealed that the usage prefix was never written when args were empty.
feedback.wasted_effort: Setting up pmdb didn't help - the trace was too minimal (only root call recorded) to be useful for this straightforward code path issue. Direct code reading and simple testing would have been faster.
pmdb_problems: pmdb-record produced a trace with only the root() call despite recording 1 observation - no Click functions were captured
show functions returned no output, providing no visibility into what was recorded
No diagnostic message indicating why Click methods weren't captured (e.g., are they lambdas, cached, in a different module?)
pmdb_wishes: Diagnostic output when no functions are recorded, explaining possible reasons
Automatic reporting of which modules/functions were instrumented before running
Better documentation of what types of functions are NOT recorded (lambdas, cached, async generators)
other_wishes: None - the straightforward approach of reading code and writing targeted tests was sufficient and faster than trace debugging would have been

claim.cause: The help hint used ctx.help_option_names[0] ('-h') even when the command's own option shadowed it, instead of using a name from the command's actual help option.

feedback.approach: I grepped src/click for 'for help' and help_option_names, which led straight to UsageError.show building the hint from ctx.help_option_names[0]. Then I read Command.get_help_option_names and get_help_option, and saw they already drop names that the command's params shadow. I changed the hint to use the resolved help option's opts[0], and made get_help_option_names keep the original order instead of going through a set.
feedback.key_step: Reading exceptions.py lines 77-83 and seeing that it uses ctx.help_option_names[0] directly, even though get_help_option (called just above) already computes the unshadowed names.
other_wishes: I didn't re-run the test suite or mypy after adding the final set[str] annotation; a quick typecheck command noted in the repo would have made that verification trivial.

claim.cause: The error hint used the raw, unfiltered ctx.help_option_names[0] instead of the command-specific filtered help option names, so it suggested a shortcut (-h) that was actually shadowed by a local option on the subcommand.

feedback.approach: I searched the source for the "Try '...' for help" string, found it in UsageError.show() in exceptions.py, and noticed it used ctx.help_option_names[0] directly rather than the per-command filtered/deduplicated help option names that Command.get_help_option_names() computes. I compared this against get_help_option_names(), which already correctly excludes names shadowed by local options, confirming the two code paths were inconsistent. I patched exceptions.py to use the filtered names and also fixed a latent ordering bug (set iteration order) in get_help_option_names() itself, then verified with the repro script and the full test suite.
feedback.key_step: Finding that get_help_option_names() already filtered out shadowed option names correctly (used for --help rendering), while exceptions.py used the raw unfiltered ctx.help_option_names list for the error hint — the discrepancy between these two was the bug.

claim.cause: When an explicitly requested embedding method was unavailable or failed to load, the code only logged via the internal logger and never raised a Python-level warning/exception, so the hash-based fallback was adopted silently with no reliably observable signal to the caller.

feedback.approach: I read the two implicated files (embedding_generator.py and text_embedder.py) directly from the bug report, found the degrade path in TextEmbedder._initialize_model where it falls back to hash embeddings on missing/failing optional dependencies, and confirmed it only called logger.warning with no exception or standard warning. I cross-checked existing tests (test_model_switching.py, test_text_embedder.py) to see that fallback behavior itself was intentional and must be preserved, which told me the fix should add a visible warnings.warn rather than raise an exception.
feedback.key_step: Finding the existing tests that explicitly assert fallback should succeed without raising (test_fallback_on_switch_failure), which ruled out 'raise an exception' as the fix and pointed to 'emit a clear warnings.warn' as the minimal, test-compatible change.
feedback.wasted_effort: Initially considered whether to distinguish 'explicit' vs 'default' method requests, which isn't actually representable in the current API (method defaults to a string indistinguishable from an explicit pass), so that line of thought didn't lead anywhere useful.
other_wishes: A quick way to know upfront which optional dependencies (sentence-transformers, fastembed) are installed in the sandbox would have saved a verification step later in the session.

claim.cause: The function did not handle FileNotFoundError when checking permissions on non-existent files, causing the plugin to crash during album imports with invalid path characters.

feedback.approach: I traced the FileNotFoundError from the stack trace directly to the check_permissions function, which was calling os.stat() without handling the case where the file doesn't exist. I reproduced the issue with a simple Python test to confirm the problem, then implemented a minimal fix by catching FileNotFoundError and returning True.
feedback.key_step: Reading the check_permissions function and recognizing that os.stat() raises FileNotFoundError when the path doesn't exist - this immediately suggested the fix.
feedback.wasted_effort: I spent time exploring what syspath does and looking at utility functions, which was unnecessary since the error location was clear from the stack trace.
other_wishes: Ability to inspect the database to see what exact path was stored for the failing item (though the error message was sufficient)
A concrete example of what the invalid path character was (though not necessary to fix the issue)

claim.cause: the finally block unlinked the temp file without closing it first when an exception occurred before the normal close point, which raises PermissionError on Windows and masks the original exception

feedback.approach: I read the reported bug and the suggested fix, then checked the actual source file instead of assuming the described code shape was still accurate. I found the primary TypeError-causing issue (mode='wb') had already been fixed in this checkout and was covered by existing tests, so I ran the pager-related tests to confirm, then traced the remaining risk: the finally block's os.unlink still ran against a potentially-open file handle when an exception occurred before the normal close point. I wrote a test to confirm this was a real gap, applied a minimal close-before-unlink guard, and verified the test failed without the fix and passed with it.
feedback.key_step: Reading the actual current source of _tempfilepager and comparing it against the bug report's claimed code shape, which revealed the mode='wb' issue was already fixed, redirecting investigation toward the remaining finally/unlink ordering bug.
feedback.wasted_effort: Initial attempt to reproduce the exact Windows PermissionError on Linux via the report's repro script, which couldn't actually trigger the Windows-specific file-locking behavior and just confirmed the happy path worked.
other_wishes: A way to actually exercise Windows-specific file-locking semantics (e.g. a sandboxed Windows execution target or a mock filesystem that enforces open-file-unlink restrictions) would have let me directly verify the PermissionError scenario rather than relying on code inspection and a close-before-unlink invariant test.

claim.cause: The manual-search/manual-ID prompt callbacks returned the new Proposal instead of assigning it to task.candidates/task.rec, so the prompt loop (which only checks callback return values for Action) silently discarded the lookup result and kept showing the original candidates.

feedback.approach: I located the interactive import code path for manual search/ID entry in beets/ui/commands/import_/session.py, and read choose_match/choose_item alongside manual_search/manual_id. I noticed the prompt loop only applies a callback's return value when it is an importer.Action, but manual_search/manual_id instead returned a Proposal object, which was silently discarded. A nearby code comment explicitly stated the intended contract ('candidates ... will be updated in place by manual_search and manual_id, with return types as None'), confirming the two functions had drifted from that contract.
feedback.key_step: Finding the stale comment above the PromptChoice definitions stating that manual_search/manual_id were supposed to mutate task.candidates/task.rec in place and return None, which directly contradicted what the current code actually did (returning a Proposal that the caller ignores).
feedback.wasted_effort: A few early greps for Proposal/candidates usage and changelog entries for #6925/#6685 that didn't turn up anything, since this isn't a git repo and the changelog doesn't reference PR numbers directly.
other_wishes: Since this wasn't a git repo, having the actual PR #6925 diff or commit history available would have let me directly confirm the before/after behavior instead of inferring it from a comment.

Reading EmbeddingGenerator.__init__ showed it builds TextEmbedder only from config['text'] and drops top-level kwargs. feedback.key_step: Running EmbeddingGenerator(method='sentence_transformers') and printing text_embedder.method gave 'fastembed', and the logged warning named fastembed instead of sentence-transformers.
feedback.wasted_effort: Not much: some initial reading of text_embedder.py's init/get_method, which the issue pointed to but which was not the actual root cause.
other_wishes: A way to tell quickly whether the two failing test_embedding_providers tests fail on the unmodified code too (e.g. a git baseline; the directory was not a git repo, so I couldn't just stash and rerun)
Clarity in the issue about whether raising or warning is preferred on fallback

claim.cause: relplot builds its legend only from user-passed kwargs, so when linewidth isn't given _scatter_legend_artist uses a marker edge width of 0, which makes outline-only markers like 'x' invisible in the legend.

feedback.approach: I grepped for the legend artist code and read _scatter_legend_artist and the legend-building code in relplot. A quick reproduction script compared legend-handle markeredgewidth between relplot and scatterplot, and monkeypatching the artist factory showed which kwargs it received. That showed relplot only forwards linewidth when the user passes it, so the edge width falls back to 0.
feedback.key_step: Seeing `"markeredgewidth": kws.pop("linewidth", 0)` in _scatter_legend_artist alongside relplot's common_kws filter, which only includes user-supplied kwargs, then confirming relplot handles had edge width 0 while scatterplot (on a fresh axes) had 0.8.
feedback.wasted_effort: My first repro ran scatterplot on the same pyplot axes as the relplot, so the scatterplot legend also showed width 0. That sent me checking normalize_kwargs and handler_map before I realized the comparison was contaminated.
other_wishes: A rendered-image check (e.g., saving the legend to PNG and viewing it) to confirm the visual fix directly rather than only via markeredgewidth values

claim.cause: manual_search/manual_id returned a Proposal instead of writing it to task.candidates/task.rec, so choose_match/choose_item discarded the manual lookup result and kept showing the original candidates

feedback.wasted_effort: Briefly considered whether ImportTask.lookup_candidates (which only supports search_ids) should be reused for both manual_search and manual_id before realizing it didn't support artist/name search and that direct assignment in the two functions was the minimal fix.
other_wishes: Git history/blame would have been very useful to directly see the diff introduced by #6925 instead of inferring the regression from a code comment and static reading — but this wasn't a git repo so that option was unavailable.

claim.cause: TextEmbedder did not track when explicitly requested embedding methods failed to load, allowing silent downgrade to fallback without raising an error.

feedback.approach: I read the bug report to understand the issue (silent downgrade without error), then explored the codebase structure to locate the EmbeddingGenerator and TextEmbedder classes. This gap between the requested and actual method revealed that the code had no mechanism to distinguish between 'intentional fallback' and 'unintentional fallback due to unavailable library'.
feedback.wasted_effort: I spent time investigating test failures in test_embedding_providers.py which turned out to be pre-existing issues due to missing fastembed/sentence-transformers dependencies in the test environment, not caused by my changes. claim.cause: relplot built its legend from raw user kwargs without replicating scatterplot's default edge-linewidth computation, so unfilled markers like 'x' got markeredgewidth=0 and vanished from the legend

feedback.approach: I traced the legend-rendering code path for relplot, comparing the axes-level scatterplot() (which worked) to the figure-level relplot() (which didn't). I instrumented _scatter_legend_artist with a trace wrapper to print the actual kwargs it received, which revealed that no 'linewidth' key was being passed at all for the relplot case, unlike the axes-level function.
feedback.key_step: Monkey-patching _scatter_legend_artist to print its received kwargs and comparing against the axes-level scatterplot() output, which showed relplot's legend-building code never included the computed default linewidth, defaulting markeredgewidth to 0.
feedback.wasted_effort: Initial manual reasoning about matplotlib's Line2D default edgecolor/facecolor behavior for unfilled markers was unnecessary once I actually instrumented and ran the code to see real values.
other_wishes: A quick way to diff kwargs/attrs flowing through two similar code paths (axes-level vs figure-level) would have shortened the manual monkey-patch/trace step.

claim.cause: Legend marker edge width defaulted to 0 when no linewidth was passed, which is invisible for unfilled/line-art markers like 'x' since they have no face color to render instead.

feedback.approach: I traced marker rendering logic in seaborn's relational.py and utils.py, then empirically tested with reproduction scripts using synthetic data (since network access to the penguins dataset was unavailable) to compare marker edge widths between the 'x' and 'X' cases. By instrumenting the code with print statements and monkeypatching, I discovered that relplot's figure-level legend construction uses a separate code path from the axes-level scatterplot, and this path never receives the computed linewidth that makes unfilled markers visible.
feedback.key_step: Printing the actual markeredgewidth values on the legend handles (mew=0 for 'x') and then tracing why: discovering relplot() rebuilds legend common_kws from raw user kwargs at line ~870 of relational.py, bypassing the per-axes linewidth computation that normally runs in _ScatterPlotter.plot().
feedback.wasted_effort: An initial monkeypatch-based trace gave confusing/contradictory output (dict missing keys I expected) because I didn't realize relplot has two distinct legend-building code paths; I had to add a raw debug print directly in the file to resolve the confusion.
other_wishes: A local/offline copy of the seaborn-data datasets (penguins.csv etc.) bundled with the repo or test fixtures, since no network access made reproducing the exact tutorial example impossible and required fabricating synthetic data instead.

A way to quickly diff 'what kwargs reach legend construction' vs 'what kwargs reach actual plotting' would have shortened the trace — e.g. a debug/verbose mode in seaborn that logs kws dicts at each legend-artist call site.

pmdb_problems: Syntax confusion: initially tried to use shell pipes inside pmdb commands instead of after the pmdb invocation
Output showed '<object>' for return values instead of useful details about Line2D properties
The function call tree didn't make it obvious that markeredgewidth was the problem
pmdb_wishes: Better rendering of object return values (show key properties like marker, markeredgewidth, etc.)
A way to easily inspect nested object properties in where clauses
Example queries for common debugging patterns (e.g., 'show me all calls where return value property X != expected Y')
other_wishes: Direct matplotlib rendering capability to verify visual changes without saving to files
Interactive debugger that could show matplotlib's internal rendering behavior for markers
Better matplotlib documentation about line-art vs filled marker rendering in legends

claim.cause: When no linewidth was passed (as in relplot's legend), _scatter_legend_artist set markeredgewidth to 0, so outline-only markers like 'x' were drawn invisibly in the legend.

feedback.approach: I read the scatter plotting and legend code in relational.py and utils.py. Then I printed the legend handle properties for scatterplot and for relplot side by side. relplot's legend handles had markeredgewidth 0 while scatterplot's had 0.8. I traced that to the fallback default in _scatter_legend_artist, used when relplot passes no linewidth.
feedback.key_step: Printing get_markeredgewidth() on relplot's legend handles showed 0 (versus 0.8 for scatterplot), which pointed straight to the `kws.pop("linewidth", 0)` default.
feedback.wasted_effort: I first reproduced with scatterplot instead of relplot. It rendered correctly, which cost one round trip before I tried relplot.
other_wishes: A way to render the legend to an image and view it, to confirm the visual fix directly rather than by checking properties

claim.cause: set_permissions() called os.stat/os.chmod on file and directory paths without checking they still exist, so a path that was never written/had been removed raised an uncaught FileNotFoundError that aborted the whole import

feedback.approach: I started from the traceback pointing at beetsplug/permissions.py, hypothesized the title's literal '/' character was causing beets to write files into an unintended nested directory, then spent most of the session rigorously testing that hypothesis (unicode slash-lookalikes, asciify_path/unidecode interactions, template substitution internals, move/store ordering) using real beets import pipelines in a Python REPL. None of these reproduced a mismatch between the DB-recorded item.path and the actual file on disk, so I concluded the robust fix was to make the permissions plugin tolerate a missing file instead of crashing, and wrote a regression test to confirm the crash and the fix.
feedback.key_step: Running a full real import (AsIsImporterMixin + permissions plugin) with a title containing '/' and observing that the file was correctly sanitized and item.path matched the real file — this ruled out the path-sanitization theory and redirected effort to hardening the plugin itself.
feedback.wasted_effort: A large amount of time was spent speculatively tracing unidecode/asciify_path, Unicode look-alike slash characters, and importer move/cleanup ordering, trying to construct an exact root-cause reproduction of a nested-directory mismatch that never actually reproduced with the current codebase.
other_wishes: Access to the actual MusicBrainz release metadata (no network access) to know the exact title string, which would have let me confirm or rule out the path-sanitization theory definitively instead of guessing at Unicode look-alikes

A way to run the actual reported beets version (2.14.1) against this exact scenario to see if the described crash is a known/fixed upstream issue, to avoid redundant verification work in the installed (possibly patched) repo snapshot

feedback.approach: I read the permissions plugin traceback and hypothesized the title field's literal '/' character wasn't being sanitized into a safe path, then traced beets' path-building pipeline (FormattedMapping, destination(), asciify_path, legalize_path) to see where that sanitization happens. I empirically tested many scenarios (literal slash in title, asciify-introduced slash via unidecode, ID3v2.3 multi-value TIT2 frames joined by mutagen with '/') through both direct API calls and the full real import pipeline, and all were correctly sanitized by the current code. Since I could not reproduce an actual path-generation bug, I concluded the robust fix was to make the permissions plugin itself resilient to a missing file (log a warning instead of crashing the whole import), which directly matches the reported symptom and the fact that disabling the plugin eliminated the error.
feedback.key_step: Discovering via mutagen testing that ID3v2.3 TIT2 frames with multiple text values get joined with '/' by mutagen, which explained exactly how a literal slash could appear in a title tag in the real world — but even after confirming this mechanism, the core beets destination-building logic handled it correctly, which pushed me toward the defensive-fix conclusion.
feedback.wasted_effort: A very large amount of time was spent hypothesizing and testing unicode/asciify-based slash-introduction theories (division slash, fraction slash, fullwidth solidus, NFC normalization edge cases) and manually re-deriving beets' template/path-sanitization pipeline from scratch, all of which turned out robust and didn't reveal the bug; this could have been shortened significantly with better tooling to directly observe the actual failing call in the real scenario.
other_wishes: Access to the actual MusicBrainz release/track metadata (no network access) to know the exact literal title string, instead of having to guess and reconstruct plausible candidates
A way to record/replay the user's actual failing scenario (e.g. a bundled reproduction script or fixture) rather than reconstructing the import pipeline conditions from scratch

Since pmdb was mentioned as available, clearer upfront guidance on when it's actually the right tool versus when a scenario (missing external data, no concrete failing input) makes it inapplicable, so I don't default to manual reasoning for too long before reconsidering

claim.cause: Unfilled markers require non-zero markeredgewidth to be visible in legend; the function now defaults markeredgewidth to 1 for unfilled markers when linewidth is not explicitly specified.

feedback.approach: I explored the project structure and identified the relplot function, then traced through the scatter plot legend creation code. I created test scripts to compare how matplotlib handles the lowercase 'x' marker (unfilled) versus uppercase 'X' (filled), discovering that unfilled markers require markeredgewidth > 0 to be visible. I then examined the _scatter_legend_artist function and found it was defaulting markeredgewidth to 0.
feedback.key_step: Testing `mpl.markers.MarkerStyle('x').is_filled()` which returned False, revealing that unfilled markers need special handling in legend rendering. Additionally, confirming that Line2D objects with marker='x' and markeredgewidth=0 don't render the marker in legends, but markeredgewidth=1 does.
feedback.wasted_effort: I spent time examining the StyleMapping class in _base.py and the unique_markers function, which weren't directly related to the issue. I also created multiple test scripts before narrowing down the exact problem location.
other_wishes: Access to a Python debugger (pdb) for stepping through code execution
Better matplotlib documentation on marker rendering in legends, especially for unfilled markers
Type hints in seaborn codebase to clarify expected object attributes

claim.cause: EmbeddingGenerator dropped top-level method kwargs before they reached TextEmbedder, and TextEmbedder silently fell back to hash embeddings on load failure with no signal distinguishing an explicit request from the implicit default

feedback.approach: I read both files named in the bug report, then directly reproduced the reported scenario by constructing EmbeddingGenerator(method="sentence_transformers") and inspecting the resulting object's attributes, which immediately showed the method kwarg never reached the TextEmbedder. I then traced why TextEmbedder itself silently falls back without any signal, and checked existing tests and other call sites to understand which behaviors were safe to change versus load-bearing.
feedback.key_step: Running EmbeddingGenerator(method='sentence_transformers') interactively and printing eg.text_embedder.method showed it was still 'fastembed', revealing that EmbeddingGenerator.__init__ only reads config.get('text', {}) and silently drops top-level kwargs.
feedback.wasted_effort: Manually reconstructing and diffing 'original' file versions for regression testing since the repo had no git history to rely on (git status: not a repo) — had to hand-write reverse-patches with Python string replacement to safely A/B test against baseline.
other_wishes: Having git initialized (even a single baseline commit) would have made regression comparison trivial instead of manually reconstructing pre-edit file contents for diffing.

A quick way to know which optional dependencies (sentence-transformers, fastembed, gensim, faiss) are intentionally absent in the sandbox vs. missing by accident would have saved time distinguishing pre-existing failures from regressions.
